title: Projectile event where instantaneous velocity is perpendicular to a reference velocity

authority_basis.claim_scope: Repository-backed SBA04 atom introduces the component dot-product zero test and applies v(t) dot u = 0 to perpendicular-velocity events.

concepts.statement: Two nonzero velocity vectors are perpendicular when their component dot product is zero; for projectile events this condition must be imposed on velocity vectors evaluated in one common frame.
concepts.why_required: Perpendicularity is a vector relation involving both components, not a rule that one component must vanish.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Learners may confuse the perpendicular event with the apex or force one component to zero.

conditions: Both vectors expressed in the same orthogonal frame
Both vectors refer to the intended event/reference states

model_conditions.condition: Both velocity vectors are represented by components in the same orthogonal coordinate frame.
model_conditions.physical_reason: A component dot product is meaningful only after the vector components share one basis.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Components from different frames cannot be combined term-by-term.

representations.semantic_geometry: A reference velocity arrow and an instantaneous velocity arrow are shown perpendicular, with their component pairs written in the same x-y basis and linked to the zero dot product.
must_not_imply: perpendicularity means one component is zero
the perpendicular event is automatically the apex
representations.verification_method: Substitute the signed component pairs and verify the scalar dot product equals zero at the claimed event.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify the two velocity vectors whose perpendicular relation is requested and express both in one frame.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The wrong event vector or mixed-frame components can be compared.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Translate perpendicularity into the signed component dot-product equation equal to zero.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Perpendicularity may be replaced by an unrelated component-zero condition.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Insert the projectile velocity evolution only after the vector condition is established, then solve and verify the event time.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Algebra can begin without preserving the physical perpendicularity condition.

required_transformations.description: Translate a right-angle relation between two velocity vectors into a component dot-product condition before solving the projectile event.
Substitute the time-evolving projectile components only after the vector constraint is formed, solve the perpendicular-velocity event, and verify the zero dot product at the resulting state.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Two velocity vectors are perpendicular only when one of the components of one vector is zero.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Horizontal and vertical vectors are familiar perpendicular examples and apex problems feature vy=0.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Vectors (1,1) and (1,-1) are perpendicular although neither component is zero.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show a slanted perpendicular vector pair with both component pairs nonzero.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Use u_x v_x+u_y v_y=0 as the general perpendicular test.
misconceptions.verification: Compute the dot product of the counterexample and confirm it is zero.

problem_families.name: Perpendicular-velocity projectile event
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write the two velocity component pairs and impose their dot product equal to zero before substituting time evolution.
fatal_errors: start algebra before defining the two vectors
